section_summary.extract_value: This Results section presents findings from a moderation analysis examining how attachment to God moderates the relationship between social comparison (body, eating, and exercise) and body appreciation in women (N = 186 and N = 164 for different analyses). Body comparison and eating comparison were negatively related to body appreciation, with these relationships being conditional upon God attachment anxiety. Exercise comparison showed conditional relationships with both attachment anxiety and avoidance dimensions. The complete models explained substantial variance in body appreciation (40-51%).

section_summary.extract_value: This results section presents descriptive statistics and intercorrelations for a single study (N=186) examining the relationship between body appreciation, social comparison, and attachment to God in women. Table 1 shows that body appreciation was negatively correlated with body, eating, and exercise comparisons (r=-.61, -.48, -.45 respectively) and with BMI (r=-.30). The text then describes three separate moderation analyses testing whether God attachment anxiety and avoidance moderate the relationship between each type of social comparison and body appreciation, with results indicating that attachment anxiety significantly moderates the effect of body and exercise comparisons on body appreciation.

section_summary.extract_value: This Results section presents findings from a single study examining how God attachment dimensions moderate the relationship between social comparison and body appreciation in women (N = 164). Three separate moderation analyses were conducted (Models 1–3) testing body comparison, eating comparison, and exercise comparison as predictors of body appreciation, with God attachment anxiety and avoidance as moderators and BMI and self-rated religiosity as covariates. The results show that social comparison variables negatively predict body appreciation, and this relationship is conditional upon God attachment anxiety (and in the exercise model, also avoidance).
